proposals.note: Cyclic-symmetric block exploiting the S6 node-relabeling symmetry of graph connectivity. Three entangling patterns at different graph distances: (1) RZZ nearest-neighbor ring (distance-1) with tied theta1 directly couples to Z_iZ_j readout observables; (2) fixed CZ gates on the three antipodal pairs (0,3),(1,4),(2,5) providing distance-3 entanglement without consuming parameters; (3) RZZ skip-two ring (distance-2) with tied theta3. Uniform RY(theta2) on all qubits provides local processing. The 6-cycle generator (0,1,2,3,4,5) is verified invariant: RZZ ring maps to itself, RY set maps to itself, CZ antipodal set maps to itself (CZ is symmetric so CZ(3,0)=CZ(0,3)), and RZZ skip-two ring maps to itself. Only 3 trainable parameters keep the block well-conditioned while the feature map supplies the edge-specific asymmetry. 21 gates, 3 params, 2 repeats x 2 layers gives 84 gate applications total.

proposals.note: 15-gate block with (0,3) transposition symmetry (order-2 group). Single-qubit RY on all 6 qubits (tied on 0/3, independent on 1,2,4,5) gives 5 params. Paired controlled rotations CRX(1,0)/CRX(1,3), CRY(2,0)/CRY(2,3), CRY(4,0)/CRY(4,3) share a control qubit and have disjoint targets, so each pair commutes and the block is exactly invariant under the swap. CZ(0,3) and CNOT(5,0)/CNOT(5,3) complete the entangling structure. 8 trainable params total, matching the best prior (c0002) while adding two extra entangling pairs for richer connectivity detection. The transposition regularises the parameter space without over-constraining, and the CZ/CNOT pair provides a fixed entangling backbone that the feature-map re-uploading can exploit across layers.

proposals.note: Block is built in 3 paired sub-layers respecting the involution (0 1)(2 3)(4 5). Each gate on a wire in {0,2,4} has a mirror gate on {1,3,5} with the same parameter, guaranteeing exact equivariance. Entangling structure: two CNOT chains (0→2→4 and 1→3→5) plus a closing CNOT(4,0)/CNOT(5,1) create a 3-cycle per half; RZZ gates add diagonal entanglement between the halves. Six RY rotations (tied in pairs) provide single-qubit mixing. 8 trainable params, 24 gates. The connectivity task is invariant under any node permutation, so this Z2 relabeling is label-preserving. Prior verifier failure was due to gate structure not matching the claimed symmetry; here every gate is explicitly paired.

proposals.note: 22-gate block with 8 trainable params, invariant under transposition (1,4). Structure: 6 RY rotations (tied t0 on {0,5}, t1 on {1,4}), 7 CNOTs forming a ring-like entangling pattern symmetric under 1<->4, and 9 RZZ gates creating pairwise correlations. RZZ params tied in symmetry orbits: f1 covers edges to nodes 0/3 (outer ring), f2 covers edges to node 2, f3 is the self-symmetric 2-3 edge, f4 covers edges to node 5. The ring topology 0-1-2-3-4-5 with chord 1-3 ensures every node is reachable, matching the connectivity-detection task. Fewer gates than c0007 (22 vs 24) with same param count (8) but richer RZZ structure (9 vs 4) to better feed the Z_iZ_j readout observables. Hypothesis: connectivity label is invariant under any node relabeling; verified that sigma=(1,4) preserves both circuit equivariance and label mapping.

proposals.note: 23-gate block with 8 params structured as: (1) per-pair RY rotations encoding input, (2) intra-pair RZZ coupling within {0,1},{2,3},{4,5}, (3-5) inter-pair RZZ coupling connecting all three pairs, (6) second per-pair RY, (7) CNOT propagation from pair-0 to pair-1. The three-pair architecture mirrors the graph structure: intra-pair RZZ detects within-pair edge presence, inter-pair RZZ detects cross-pair edges, and CNOTs propagate connectivity info toward the readout qubits. No hypothesis claimed to avoid equivariance risk with the fixed feature map; the block relies on the trainable linear readout over 21 Z/ZiZj observables to extract the connectivity signal. Gate count kept at 23/24 for expressivity while staying within budget.

proposals.note: Cyclically symmetric 24-gate block with 4 tied params. Structure: (1) uniform RY rotation sets measurement basis; (2) 6 CNOTs propagate info around the 6-cycle; (3) 6 RZZ on cycle edges detect nearest-neighbor connectivity; (4) 3 RZZ on diameter edges (0,3),(1,4),(2,5) probe long-range connectivity; (5) 3 CRX on diameters add controllable cross-talk for path detection. The C6 symmetry (generator 0->1->2->3->4->5->0) matches the node-relabeling symmetry of the connectivity task. Compared to c0007 (risk 0.5034), this trades some CNOT depth for RZZ+CRX on diameter edges, which more directly encodes the 'is there a path across the graph' question. Fewer params (4 vs 8) reduces overfitting risk while the 4x block repetition (2 layers x 2 repeats) provides sufficient depth.

proposals.note: Strictly cyclic-equivariant block: 4 layers of 6 gates each (RY, CNOT-ring, RY, RZZ-ring) all sharing one parameter per layer. The 6-cycle (0→1→2→3→4→5→0) maps every gate to another gate in the same layer with the same parameter, guaranteeing exact equivariance. CNOT ring propagates connectivity info around the cycle; RZZ ring adds pairwise phase entanglement. 24 gates, 3 params, minimal risk of equivariance failure unlike prior proposals where gate sets were not closed under the claimed permutation.

proposals.note: 24-gate block equivariant under the 6-cycle (0,1,2,3,4,5). Structure: 6 RY (1 param) → 6 RZZ nearest-neighbour (1 param) → 6 RZZ next-nearest (1 param) → 3 RZZ diametric (1 param) → 3 CZ diametric (fixed). All RZZ/CZ gates are diagonal and mutually commuting, so the 6-cycle merely permutes gates within each commuting group, leaving every group-product invariant; the RY group is likewise a product of commuting single-qubit rotations. Four trainable parameters cover all three edge-distance classes (d=1,2,3) plus local rotations, giving the readout Z_i and Z_iZ_j observables direct access to pairwise correlations at every graph distance. The fixed CZ diametric gates seed long-range entanglement that the trainable RZZ layers can modulate. With 2 layers × 2 repeats the block is applied 4 times, allowing connectivity information to propagate around the 6-ring and across diameters. The 6-cycle hypothesis regularises the parameter space while preserving the full S_6 label symmetry of the connectivity task.
